newsitem.title: USA: Calif. pension fund cancels $825 mln UBS contract.
newsitem.headline: Calif. pension fund cancels $825 mln UBS contract.

text.p: Los Angeles County Employees Retirement Association -- one of California's largest public pension funds -- has terminated its contract with UBS Asset Management Inc due to personnel changes at the firm, a senior association official said Thursday.
New York-based UBS Asset Management, a unit of Union Bank of Switzerland, had been managing $825 million of the association's bond assets under a contract signed in December.
But Juan Almaguer, the association's fixed-income investment officer, said the contract was terminated on May 9 because of personnel changes at the firm's New York office.
"Several key investment professionals left UBS and went to a competitor so we decided it was in our best interest to take the assets away," he said.

Almaguer added that the association's decision to terminate its contract with UBS was "absolutely not" related to allegations that Swiss banks hoarded unclaimed wealth of Holocaust victims. "It had nothing to do with that," he said.
UBS Asset Management declined to comment on its personnel changes. The firm said the loss of the Los Angeles contract had reduced its assets under management to about $21 billion from $22 billion.
Almaguer said the pension fund has already distributed the $825 million formerly managed by UBS to IDS Advisory Group, Loomis Sayles & Co, and Western Asset Management Co.
The association manages a $21 billion pension fund for 120,000 public employees, retirees and their families.
